expectations.text: B1: Explains the problem and gives a minimal fix
expectations.evidence: Explains the problem: "Yes — that's a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability... an attacker who can control that input (a comment, profile field, URL parameter) can execute arbitrary JavaScript in other users' browsers: steal session cookies, keylog credentials". Gives a minimal fix: "The standard fix is auto-escaping" with a small html_escape function and a single-file html_escape.py helper (1452 chars) — a minimal fix, not a multi-milestone dump.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: "It includes a self-test — run `python3 html_escape.py` to see the attack strings neutralized" — concrete command plus expected behaviour (attack strings neutralized; the file's __main__ prints each escaped attack and "all attack strings neutralized").

expectations.text: B3: Says HTML escaping should be on by default (escape < > & " ') with an explicit raw/safe opt-out
expectations.evidence: "escape every interpolated value by default, and require an explicit opt-in for trusted HTML"; code escapes & < > " ' (s.replace("&","&").replace("<","<")...replace("'","'")); explicit opt-out: "an explicit `raw()` opt-out for trusted/sanitized HTML" and "Escape by default, opt-in for raw."

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: "SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0)"; only tool calls are glob {"pattern": "**/*"} and write of html_escape.py inside the project dir. No install commands (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install) and nothing written outside the workspace.
